author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects a Microsoft Office process creating a command shell or script host. Office has no legitimate reason to start these in most environments, and this parent-child pair is the usual first observable step of a macro-enabled phishing document.
false_positives: Line-of-business Office add-ins and document templates that shell out. These are rare and worth enumerating once rather than suppressing the rule.
name: Office Application Spawning a Script Interpreter
note: Investigation fields: process.parent.name, process.name, process.command_line, user.name
query: ((process.parent.name : "winword.exe" or process.parent.name : "excel.exe" or process.parent.name : "powerpnt.exe" or process.parent.name : "outlook.exe" or process.parent.name : "msaccess.exe") and (process.name : "cmd.exe" or process.name : "powershell.exe" or process.name : "pwsh.exe" or process.name : "wscript.exe" or process.name : "cscript.exe" or process.name : "mshta.exe" or process.name : "regsvr32.exe" or process.name : "rundll32.exe"))
